content.text:
I submitted **index 16** (Sb 0.66 / Zn 0.34, the ZnSb₂O₆ ratio) as the best composition. Its EQE was very low, 9.8×10⁻⁴ %, but it was the highest of the three I measured.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.31 | 4.8×10⁻⁴ |
| 16 | 0.66 | 9.8×10⁻⁴ |
| 25 | 0.86 | −3.3×10⁻³ (no photoresponse) |

- **The merit budget was only 3 measurements**, so I tested one composition each from the low-Sb, middle and high-Sb parts of the 30-sample line. The other 27 were never measured, and a better composition could sit between those points.
- **XRD didn't help.** I used 3 of the 5 XRD scans. All three samples showed the same main peaks, and none matched any of the database phases well (best similarity about 0.33). Composition trends and the EQE results drove the choice, not phase identification.
- **The illumination is 2.1 eV,** which is probably below the band gap of most Zn–Sb oxides. That fits with every signal being tiny, so the gap between index 16 and index 4 is small in absolute terms.
